articles.title: Anthropic’s AI Agent Evaluation Framework Explains How to Test Agents Before Deployment
articles.excerpt: Anthropic has published a detailed framework for evaluating AI agents before and during deployment. Its Engineering Blog guide to AI agent evaluations presents a nine-step roadmap for building evaluat…
articles.body: Anthropic has published a detailed framework for evaluating AI agents before and during deployment. Its Engineering Blog guide to AI agent evaluations presents a nine-step roadmap for building evaluation programs across coding, conversational, research and computer-use agents. The central message is practical: agent quality cannot be judged reliably through occasional demonstrations. Teams need repeatable tests, robust scoring and ongoing monitoring to understand what an agent can do, where it fails and whether it is ready for a real workflow. The guide, titled Demystifying evals for AI agents and published January 9, 2026, treats evaluations as a core part of product development rather than a final pre-launch check.

articles.excerpt: Hey everyone! Mahdi Shamlou here — back with another LeetCode problem! After solving LeetCode #9 — Palindrome Number, today I want to share my experience solving Problem #10 — Regular Expression Match…
articles.body: Hey everyone! Mahdi Shamlou here — back with another LeetCode problem! After solving LeetCode #9 — Palindrome Number , today I want to share my experience solving Problem #10 — Regular Expression Matching . This problem was a little different from the previous ones. At first, I thought about checking characters one by one, but after understanding the behavior of . and * , I realized that I needed a different approach. Let's see how I approached it. Problem Statement Given an input string s and a pattern p , implement regular expression matching with support for: . Matches any single character. * Matches zero or more of the preceding element. The matching should cover the entire input string, not just a part of it.

articles.body: Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, and Cline regularly clone repositories or install community SKILL.md , .cursorrules , CLAUDE.md , and mcp.json files directly into their local workspaces. Unlike passive documentation, agent instruction files and MCP configurations are executable control planes . When an AI coding agent has bash and filesystem tool access, a malicious or compromised skill file can instruct the agent to read .env.local , exfiltrate credentials, or execute arbitrary shell commands.

articles.body: We changed the Google Play title of a small Android app (a reverse chord finder for guitar) in four languages at once: Danish, Italian, Russian and Swedish. Two days later we had to decide: keep the new titles or roll them back. The tempting reading was "the app now shows up in all four countries, it worked". That reading was wrong, or at least it answered a different question. This post shows the raw numbers from that verdict (measured 3 November 2026) plus a second one on short descriptions (measured 4 November 2026), and the method we now use so that a rank change is not mistaken for demand.

articles.title: Ваш апскейл в 4K выглядит хуже, потому что вы выбрали не тот пресет, а не потому что 4K плохой
articles.excerpt: Почти каждый, кто говорит «ИИ-апскейл испортил мне видео», прав насчёт симптома и ошибается насчёт виновника. Они прогнали клип 360p через 4-кратную модель, получили файл 1440p с пластиковым видом и р…
articles.body: Почти каждый, кто говорит «ИИ-апскейл испортил мне видео», прав насчёт симптома и ошибается насчёт виновника. Они прогнали клип 360p через 4-кратную модель, получили файл 1440p с пластиковым видом и решили, что апскейл — развод. Это не так. Что произошло на самом деле: они применили одну модель восстановления к материалу, которому нужно было четыре разных. Выход в 4K — не готовый продукт, а последний шаг цепочки, и каждый пресет в этой цепочке оптимизирован под свой тип повреждения. В этой статье — пять пресетов, которые я использую чаще всего, что каждый делает на уровне пикселей, и правила выбора. Если читать только одно — прыгайте к таблице в конце. Но рассуждение важнее таблицы, потому что пресеты взаимодействуют.

articles.title: In-Situ Recursive Discussions for AI-Generated Markdown (Zero-Login Demo)
articles.excerpt: Traditional AI chat interfaces (like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) have a fundamental UX flaw: everything flows to the bottom. If an LLM writes a 600-word response and you have a doubt about a sentence…
articles.body: Traditional AI chat interfaces (like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini) have a fundamental UX flaw: everything flows to the bottom. If an LLM writes a 600-word response and you have a doubt about a sentence at the top, you are forced to scroll to the very bottom, manually re-quote the text, and ask your question—completely breaking your reading flow. To solve this, I built @zefina/inline-discussions: an open-source React engine that brings Google Docs-style contextual threads directly inside AI Markdown responses.

articles.title: 60 years ago the Leonid meteor shower produced 144,000 meteors per hour. Could it happen again?
articles.excerpt: 60 years ago, the Leonid meteor shower unleashed one of the most spectacular meteor storms in recorded history. As the 2026 peak approaches, here's what skywatchers can expect.
articles.body: This year marks a rather auspicious anniversary for meteor watchers. Sixty years ago , one of the most stupendous Leonid meteor displays lit up the predawn skies over the central and western U.S. So, what will the 2026 Leonids bring us? And what might they bring in the years to come? The Leonid meteor shower is one of the most celebrated of the year's annual displays of "shooting stars." The mere mention of the Leonids usually elicits mental images of a sky filled with shooting stars pouring down through the sky like rain. Such meteor storms have indeed occurred with the Leonids, such as in 1833 and 1966 when meteor rates of tens of thousands per hour were observed.

An Electron rocket topped with a private Japanese Earth-observing satellite is scheduled to launch from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site on Saturday, during a window that opens at 12:30 a.m. EST (0530 GMT; 6:30 p.m. local time). The mission, which Rocket Lab calls "The Mountain God Rises," will be the 100th to date for the California-based company. articles.body: In many of the biggest science fiction franchises, conversing with alien races is an absolute doddle. In " Star Trek ", universal translators come as standard, while C-3PO has spent the last 49 years reminding everyone in "Star Wars" that he's fluent in over six million forms of communication. But in "Arrival" — which was released 10 years ago in November 2016 — making first contact proves to be rather more challenging than maintaining your Duolingo streak. In fact, working out how to establish a dialogue with extraterrestrial visitors becomes the whole point of this powerful and heartbreaking story, as the fate of planet Earth hinges on the interpretation of a single noun.

articles.body: LOS ANGELES — The California Science Center officially opened its brand-new Samuel Oschin Air & Space Center to the public today (Nov. 13). articles.title: Think you have good eyesight? Try counting the stars in the Pleiades tonight
articles.excerpt: Every November, I give myself a completely unscientific eyesight test using one of my favorite sights in the night sky — the Pleiades. How many stars can you see?
articles.body: Every autumn, I conduct an eyesight test that no reputable optometrist would understand. I go outside, find the Pleiades and count how many stars I can see. Usually I start confidently. One, two, three, four, five. Then things become contentious. Is that another star? Did I actually see it, or did I decide I ought to see it because I know it's there? I look away, look back and begin again. This is not, I should emphasize, a meaningful test of eye health. What it tests, rather, is how badly I've prepared for looking at the night sky. The Pleiades sit roughly 444 light-years away in Taurus and are right now becoming extremely convenient in the evening sky. You don't need a telescope to find them. You don't even need binoculars.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.excerpt: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
articles.body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
